topics.title: Backstage Intimacies and Rock Star Encounters
topics.summary: During a radio interview, a woman recounts numerous sexual encounters with various rock musicians including David Lee Roth, Richard Carpenter, Don Henley, Keith Moon, and members of bands like Fleetwood Mac, Van Halen, Rush, and the Who. These interactions frequently occurred backstage or within production offices facilitated by crew members, often involving multiple partners.

topics.title: Radio Host Confrontation and Editing
topics.summary: After discovering his program director, Andy, had altered a broadcast referencing competitor station kroq, radio host Gary confronts him with accusations of manipulation and threats to terminate their relationship. Chaotic phone calls from listeners further escalate the situation as they discuss similar experiences.

topics.title: Howard Disputes Editing with Program Director
topics.summary: Radio host Howard argues vehemently with his program director, Andy, over repeated edits to his show recordings referencing competitor station kroq. He accuses Andy of undermining his authority by altering the content and disrupting his career progression due to unnecessary editing.

topics.title: Radio Host Disputes Tape Edits and Accusations

topics.title: Press Conference Frustration & Stern-Letterman
topics.summary: During the broadcast, hosts dissect John and Jennifer Flowers’ press conference, expressing frustration with its lack of substantive information. A listener call reveals ongoing tensions between Howard Stern and David Letterman fueled by perceived slights during broadcasts, including a discussion about Paul Shafer.

topics.title: Secrets and Underwear - Vegas Confessions
topics.summary: During a casual conversation, Dave brings up Paul Shafer and his recent trip to Las Vegas with Mick and Keith. They discuss Shafer’s constant references to ‘show business,’ recalling the moment he found Shafer entertaining himself while observing celebrity jam sessions. The discussion then shifts to personal anecdotes of secrets kept from the air – including a story about Raquel Welch, an embarrassing incident involving a mother inspecting underwear, and concerns over a young boy's developing anatomy.
